Challenging common impugned judgment and award dated 20.06.2015, passed by Civil Judge (Sr.Dn) and Additional MACT, Koppal, in MVC Nos.185 and 186 of 2016, these appeals are filed.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of case are that on 11.01.2016 Ameena Begum was traveling as pillion rider on motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-36/W-229 along with her son Syed Zaheer on NH-63, when driver of NEKRTC bus bearing registration no.KA- 37/F-4559 drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against motorcycle causing accident.
In accident, both rider as well as pillion sustained grievous injuries and died on spot.
3. Alleging loss of dependency on account of her untimely death, her children had filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, against driver of bus and NEKRTC.
4. On contest, claim petition was opposed on all counts including contributory negligence of rider of motorcycle.
5. Tribunal framed issues.
and claimants examined three witnesses as PW1 to PW3 and got marked Exhibits P1 to P10.

Driver of NEKRTC bus was examined as RW1 and got marked photographs and CD as Exs.R1(a to d).
6.

On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of bus by its driver and claimants were held entitled for compensation of Rs.7,20,872/- with interest at 7%
p.a.

Not satisfied with quantum of compensation, claimants have preferred MFA no.100149/2019,
while aggrieved by award on negligence as well as on quantum, NEKRTC has filed MFA no.103278/2018.
7.
At out set learned counsel submitted that issue regarding contributory negligence has been decided by Division Bench of this Court in MFA no.103175/2018 disposed of on 01.12.2020.
While deciding said contention in connected claim petition arising out of same accident, negligence held against driver of NEKRTC has been confirmed.
Therefore, said point would not be available for consideration.
Appeal would therefore be confined to quantum.

8. Since both claimants as well as NEKRTC are assailing award on quantum, point that arises for consideration is:
 "Whether assessment of  compensation by tribunal calls for  modification as sought for?"
9.

Insofar as contention of learned counsel appearing for NEKRTC's that since claimants are all majors and shown to have their own occupation, they were required to be held as not dependents Syed Asif S/O. Late Abdul Gani vs Gangappa Sajjanar S/O. Shantappa on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187919929/
4
upon income of deceased, therefore claim petition was liable to be dismissed.
It is seen that deceased was mother of claimants.
It is settled law that services of household wife is held to be loss caused to family members

. Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arun Kumar Agarwal and another Vs.
National Insurance Co. Ltd. reported in (2010) 9 SCC 218 has taken note of same and held dependents would be entitled for compensation.

entities.text:
Arun Kumar Agarwal and another Vs.
National Insurance Co. Ltd. reported in (2010) 9 SCC 218
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no evidence to establish that claimants were residing separately from their mother.
10. Insofar as monthly income, though claimants have stated that deceased was working as vegetable vender and earning Rs.10,000/- per month, there is no specific evidence to substantiate same.
In absence of same, income has to be assessed on notional terms.
Notional income for year 2016 is Rs.8,750/- as per norms adopted by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in settlement of cases before Lokadalat.
Therefore, Tribunal was not justified in taking it at Rs.8,000/-.
It has to be considered at Rs.8,750/- per month.
11. Deceased was 58 years of age.
Claimants are her children.
Thus, as per formula evolved by Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 68, proper multiplier applicable would be '9'.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 68
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per ratio in Pranay Sethi case (supra), claimants would be entitled for addition of 10% towards future prospects.
Deduction towards personal expenses would have to be at 1/3 r d .
Thus, loss of dependency would be (Rs.8,750/- + 10% -1/3 X 12 X 9) Rs.6,93,000/-.

Apart from above, they would be entitled to award of Rs.40,000/- each towards parental consortium and also Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate since more than three years have lapsed after rendering decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), there has to be addition of 10% on award under conventional heads.

12. Thus, total re-assessed compensation is as follows:-
Sl.no. Heads Amount 1. Loss of dependency 6,93,000/-
 (8,750+10%-1/3X12X9)
2. Funeral expenses 15,000/-
3. Loss of estate 15,000/-
4. Loss of consortium (40000X3) 1,20,000/-
5.

Insofar as rate of interest, in case of SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. LAXMI reported in 2018(4) AKR 808 it is held that interest payable on award under Motor Vehicles Act would be as per Section 34 of Code of Civil Procedure is at 6%.

O R D E R i.
Both appeals are allowed in part.
ii. MFA no.103278/2018 filed by  NEKRTC is allowed only to extent of reduction of interest.
iii. Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to Tribunal for disbursement.
iv. MFA no.100149/2019 filed by claimants is allowed in part.
v. Claimants are entitled for  reassessed compensation of  Rs.8,58,000/- as against  Rs.7,20,872/- awarded by tribunal with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
NEKRTC is directed to deposit balance enhanced compensation within eight weeks.
vii. Ratio of apportionment between claimants as per tribunal award would apply to enhanced compensation also.
